equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR: NCI share of profit HK$15m; H1 FY2026 interim: HK$6m, NCI book HK$117m

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: below equity_5yr_cagr (2.48%) because book growth reflects retained earnings in a business whose revenue is flat and EPS is falling
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.5% vs EPS 5yr CAGR -2.3% and revenue 3yr CAGR -1.8%: book value is compounding only because ~75% payout leaves some retention, not because the business grows. Equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: FCF series is owner FCF = reported (SBC nil from FY2020, HK$32m/17m/6m in FY2017-19; interest income not stripped as net debt throughout). FY2022 FCF of 2,400 was a peak with capex at 3.2% of revenue; FY2023-24 EBITDA fell from ~HK$2.6bn to ~HK$2.0bn on lower enterprise-solutions project revenue in Macau and international SMS/voice erosion.

scenario_narratives.base: CITIC Telecom stays a flat-revenue, ~20% EBITDA-margin cash generator. Telecom services held flat in H1 FY2026 while low-margin handset sales fell; Macau 5G/enterprise and DataMall roaming growth roughly offset legacy international voice/SMS decline, and growth creeps back to ~1.5%. D&A keeps rolling off toward the ~4% capex run-rate, finance costs fall after the 2025 bond refinancing, and FCF funds a ~75% payout plus slow deleveraging.
scenario_narratives.bull: Macau mobile consolidation (SmarTone absorbed, Hutchison 3 Macau acquired and exiting by December 2026) leaves CTM one of only two operators with better pricing power; Macau's visitor economy and 'AI Macau' digitisation bring enterprise solutions back toward FY2022-23 scale; DataMall/IPX carrier services ride 5G SA and IoT/eSIM roaming; the Southeast Asia ICT push adds growth. Revenue grows 2.5-3% for five years and EBITDA margin recovers to ~22%, half-way back to the FY2022 26%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The structural erosions continue: OTT substitution of international voice/SMS hubbing, enterprise-solutions price competition (down 7.2% in FY2025), and government-mandated Macau service waivers. The fixed-voice concession, extended only to 30 September 2027 with a government termination option from October 2026, concession assets transferred to the government and ducts opened to rivals, is renewed on worse terms or folded into a legislated sector restructuring. Revenue declines ~2%/yr for three years and EBITDA margin slides to 17.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mature, low-growth Macau/HK telecom and carrier-services cash generator controlled by CITIC Group. Valued on normalised owner FCF after full lease cost, with the terminal value capped at 13x FCF rather than Gordon, because the stock has never been granted a growth multiple. The gap between value and price is mostly the market's discount for SOE control, a flat top line and concession/regulatory risk in Macau.
key_risks_to_valuation: Macau fixed-voice concession ends 30-Sep-2027; renewal terms unknown and concession ducts being opened to competitors
Continued decline of international voice/SMS hubbing (OTT substitution)
Macau mobile price competition and government-mandated service discounts
Lumpy enterprise-solutions project revenue in Macau (drove the FY2023-24 EBITDA reset)
Controlling-shareholder (CITIC) capital-allocation and minority-holder discount; interim DPS cut in H1 FY2026
FY2025 FCF flattered by working capital; normalised FCF is ~HK$1.25bn, not HK$1.9bn

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.34-2.86 HKD
data_sources.financials: 1883.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2017-FY2025, H1 FY2023-FY2026); FY2025 annual report (cash flow statement, financial review, ROU depreciation note); H1 FY2026 interim report (net debt, lease liabilities, NCI, diluted EPS note)
data_sources.qualitative: 1883.HK_Analysis.json (bull/bear cases, Macau consolidation and concession detail); FY2025 annual report and H1 FY2026 interim outlook

inputs.share_count_basis: 3,701m ordinary shares; basic = diluted per H1 FY2026 interim note (diluted EPS equals basic, no dilutive options outstanding). Held FLAT: SBC is nil since FY2020 and the company does not buy back or issue.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: no equity-settled share-based payment expense since FY2020 (FY2019 HK$5.5m, FY2018 HK$16.8m); share option scheme lapsed. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD is pegged to USD, so built off USD/HKD rates: risk-free ~4.0%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.75 for a low-growth regulated-ish telecom, +0.5pp for Macau/mainland policy exposure => cost of equity ~8.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (FY2025 effective borrowing rate after refinancing), ~3.8% after tax. Gross debt ~25% of capital at market => WACC ~7.4%, rounded to 7.5% and held identical across scenarios (risk charged in the flows, not the rate).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full lease cash payment (FY2025 capital element HK$106m + interest element HK$15m = HK$121m, 1.26% of revenue) is charged through lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (HK$281m at 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A 683 less ROU depreciation 122 = 561, 5.9% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). NCI is small (FY2025 NCI profit HK$15m of HK$935m, 1.6%; H1 FY2026 HK$6m; NCI book HK$117m). Charged once, in the equity bridge, at ~13x NCI profit (HK$180m). Calibration: FY0 component NOPAT (EBITDA 1,925 - lease 121 - D&A ex-ROU 561 = EBIT 1,243 x 85% = 1,057) ties to attributable NPAT 920 + after-tax finance costs ~130 = ~1,050.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with non-US adaptations (currency-matched WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, SBC-zero). Routing: CITIC Telecom is an operating telecom company -- CTM (Macau's incumbent full-service mobile/fixed/broadband operator, ~99% owned), international voice/SMS/data carrier hub (CITIC Telecom International / DataMall), and enterprise ICT (CPC, Acclivis in Singapore). It takes no deposits and holds no investment book, so neither the bank nor the holdco row applies. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); balance-sheet anchors are the H1 FY2026 interim (30 Jun 2026): total debt HK$2,928m (bank/other borrowings only, leases excluded), cash and deposits HK$1,780m, net debt HK$1,148m. reported_fcf = FY2025 OCF 2,266 - PP&E payments 366 = 1,900. OCF here is pre-interest (borrowing costs and lease interest sit in financing, interest received in investing), so no interest-income strip is needed and the company is net-debt anyway. FY2025 FCF is flattered by a working-capital inflow (FY2024 was 1,156; lease-adjusted 1,779 vs 1,016); the component build gives a normalised FY0 owner FCF of ~HK$1.25bn after leases, between the two. No buybacks; flat share count is a convention, not a funded outcome, but with zero SBC there is nothing to fund. Interim DPS cut to HK5.0c from HK6.0c in H1 FY2026. Terminal value is cap-bound (13x) in every scenario: Gordon at 7.5%/1.5% would be ~16.9x, a multiple an HK telecom has not traded on.

bear.narrative: International voice/SMS keeps eroding, Macau mobile ARPU is compressed by government-mandated price waivers despite in-market consolidation, the fixed-voice concession (extended only to 30-Sep-2027, government termination option from Oct-2026) is re-tendered on worse terms with ducts opened to rivals, and Macau enterprise projects stay lumpy.

base.narrative: H1 FY2026 run-rate: revenue -1.2% with telecom services flat and handset sales down; EBITDA margin held ~20% after the FY2023-24 reset. Slow recovery to 1.5% growth as Macau 5G/enterprise and DataMall roaming offset legacy voice/SMS decline.
base.da_note: D&A ex-ROU has fallen from ~8% to 5.9% of revenue as legacy network assets fully depreciate; it converges toward the 4% capex run-rate.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: Blended Macau 12% / HK 16.5% / other on EBIT; FY2025 P&L tax 193 on PBT 1,128 = 17%, cash 168. Drifts to 16% as the HK/Macau Pillar Two 15% minimum top-up applies to CITIC Group.

bull.narrative: Macau mobile consolidation (SmarTone absorbed; Hutchison 3 Macau acquired and exiting by Dec-2026) leaves CTM one of two operators and lifts pricing, Macau visitor recovery and 'AI Macau' projects return, DataMall roaming and IPX/5G SA carrier services grow; margins recover half-way to the FY2022 level.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: revenue has not grown in five years, EPS 3yr CAGR is -8%, the H1 FY2026 interim dividend was cut, and the Macau fixed-voice concession expires Sep-2027 under a single regulator. Base 50% on the current flat run-rate. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs Macau enterprise projects, roaming and SE Asia ICT to all turn at once in a business with no growth track record.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
